text: To brace for something is to get ready for something hard that you know is coming. Peru and Ecuador are bracing for the strongest El Niño in modern times.
An anomaly is something different from what is normal. Here it means how many degrees the ocean is above its usual temperature.
Staggering means so big or surprising that it is hard to believe. The scientist says this El Niño grew that fast and got that warm.
A state of emergency is an official announcement by a government that a danger is serious enough to need special actions and help.
A strategic reserve is a stockpile saved in advance for a time of shortage. Many countries store oil this way, but almost none store fertiliser.
El Niño is a warm phase of the Pacific Ocean in which the hottest water spreads from west to east. It changes weather around the tropics and beyond.
ENSO is the name for the whole seesaw of Pacific Ocean temperatures. El Niño is its warm swing.
Climatic means having to do with climate, the usual weather of a place over many years.
A seesaw is a playground board that goes up on one end while the other goes down. Here it means the climate swings back and forth between two states.
A phenomenon is something that happens in nature and can be observed. El Niño is a natural one.
To wax is to grow bigger and to wane is to shrink. Waxing and waning means rising and falling again and again, like the moon.
Proxy records are clues like tree rings that show what the weather was long ago, before people had thermometers.
A tree grows one ring each year, and wetter years make wider rings. Scientists read the rings to learn about old weather.
A forecaster is a person who predicts the weather before it happens.
A peak is the highest point. The El Niño is expected to peak, or reach its strongest, around December.
To lag behind is to come later than something else. Many effects of El Niño arrive weeks after the ocean heats up.
A drought is a long time with too little rain, which leaves land and crops dry.
Wildfires are large fires that spread quickly through forests or dry grass.
Surveillance means watching closely. Health officials use it to spot a disease early.
An outbreak is a sudden rise in cases of a disease in one area.
Rift Valley Fever is an illness spread by mosquitoes that can sicken animals and people. Heavy rains help mosquitoes multiply.
A trade bloc is a group of countries that work together to make trading with each other easier.
A water-intensive crop needs a great deal of water to grow. Rice is one.
To cultivate land is to prepare it and grow crops on it.
A whopper is something very big. The writer uses it playfully for the huge El Niño.
The mother of all something means the biggest, most extreme example of it.
A meteorologist is a scientist who studies weather.
The equator is the imaginary line around the middle of Earth, halfway between the poles.
The tropics are the warm regions on both sides of the equator.
A counterpart is someone or something that matches another in a different place. Here, coastal towns in the south match those in California.
Guayaquil is the largest city in Ecuador, a port on the Pacific coast of South America.
The norm is what is normal or usual. About 100 times the norm means 100 times the usual amount.
Sea-surface temperature is how warm the top layer of the ocean is.
A red alert is the highest warning level, telling people serious danger is near.
The World Food Programme is a United Nations group that delivers food to people facing hunger.
To reckon is to think or estimate. The agency reckons 49 million more people could go hungry.
The y-axis is the up-and-down line on a chart that shows the numbers. It had to be stretched to fit this record.
A millennium is a thousand years.
Human-driven means caused by what people do, such as burning fuels that warm the planet.
To absorb is to soak up. The ocean absorbs heat from the air like a sponge soaks up water.
Downstream means further along a chain, like people who feel the effects of a forecast after it is made.
Fertiliser is plant food that farmers spread on fields to help crops grow.
The Strait of Hormuz is a narrow stretch of sea by the Persian Gulf. Much oil and fertiliser ships through it.
To adapt is to change so you can cope with new conditions.
A temperature anomaly measures how far a temperature is above or below its usual level.
A campaigner is someone who works to persuade people to support a cause.
